title: General-Purpose Language Models vs Ridge on Protein Language Models (FLIP2 and Post-Cutoff FGFR2)
models_tested: Claude Mythos 5.2 (harness, low and high effort)
Claude Fable 5.2 (API, low and high effort)
plm_baselines: One-hot + zero-shot ridge (ESMC-6B, ESMC-600M, ESMC-300M, ESM-2 650M)
Zero-shot masked marginals / PPLL (ESMC-6B, ESMC-600M, ESMC-300M, ESM-2 650M)
One-hot ridge, nearest-neighbor, composition, random vector, untrained ESMC-300M, shuffled/permuted ESMC controls
code_and_data_released: Full code, exact prompts, answers, transcript audit, summary tables, figures, and Hub dataset publicly released.

methods.datasets: All 16 splits of the 7 FLIP2 datasets plus 2 splits (random and by_position) of a post-cutoff MaveDB screen (urn:mavedb:00001329-a-3, FGFR2 kinase domain erdafitinib resistance, published 2026-11-20 after the June 2026 Claude training cutoff).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Models receive 256 labeled training variants as plain text with the protein unnamed and rank 100 held-out queries per prompt (first 100 queries per split for Mythos 5.2 via audited single-prompt subagents; all 300 queries per split for public API models, kept strictly separate). Ridge baselines fit on the identical rounded 256 rows with leave-one-out penalty selection.
methods.controls_included: Residue/position cipher (k256_cipher), reflected labels (k256_flipped), shuffled labels (k256_shuffled), zero-shot named protein (k0_described), verbatim recall prompt (k0_recall) against 2,000 random deals, dataset recognition probe, post-cutoff FGFR2 splits, and 5 embedding-ridge controls (random, composition, untrained ESMC-300M, shuffled residues, permuted positions).
methods.compute_and_tools: No external tools or code execution (subagent transcripts audited to verify Read prompt + Write answer only). Validation effort sweep selected low effort for Mythos 5.2 (median 2,156 thinking tokens/prompt); high effort also tested on probe splits.
methods.metrics: Mean Spearman rank correlation across splits with 95% paired bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws), plus NDCG, top-decile ROC AUC, PR AUC, balanced MCC, and within-stratum Spearman.
methods.wet_lab_protocol: None (retrospective FLIP2 and prospective post-cutoff MaveDB evaluation).

key_results.notes: Pre-specified tie (3 wins, 3 losses, 10 undecided). Excluding Rhomax (driven by prior knowledge), Mythos scores 0.36 vs ridge 0.38 (-0.02, -0.07 to +0.03). Fable 5.2 API also ties best ridge on all 300 queries (0.365 vs 0.355).

key_results.benchmark: Post-cutoff FGFR2 MaveDB (2 splits, k=256, first 100 queries)
key_results.notes: Assay published 2026-11-20 after June 2026 model cutoff. Tie holds without measurement leakage (though FGFR2 sequence itself is known; cipher drops fgfr2/random from 0.662 to 0.342).

key_results.llm_model: Equal-weight rank average (Mythos 5.2 + best ESMC ridge)
key_results.baseline_score: +0.063 (+0.033 to +0.092) over Mythos; +0.077 over ridge on FLIP2
key_results.notes: Untuned equal-weight rank average beats both models with intervals excluding zero, showing complementary error profiles.

key_results.baseline_model: One-hot ridge 0.209 (vs cipher); ESMC-6B zero-shot 0.318 (vs k0)
key_results.baseline_score: Cipher beats one-hot ridge by +0.070; k0_described 0.391 vs ESMC-6B 0.318
key_results.notes: Separates true in-context learning (flipped reverses to -0.235 on 6/8 sets; cipher retains 0.278) from prior protein knowledge (Rhomax stays +0.583 when flipped and drops to -0.020 under cipher).

temporal_cutoff.evidence: FLIP2 predates the June 2026 cutoff (Zenodo 2026-01-30), so the experiment explicitly pairs FLIP2 with post-cutoff MaveDB urn:mavedb:00001329-a-3 (published 2026-11-20) plus k0_recall exact-match tests (0/400 exact continuous matches).

homology_overlap.evidence: Evaluates FLIP2's extrapolation splits (by_position, close_to_far, low_to_high, unseen wild-types/proteins) and FGFR2 by_position; post-cutoff coverage is currently one protein (FGFR2), motivating our post-cutoff MaveDB expansion.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Explicitly quantified via dataset recognition probe (Mythos named all 7 FLIP2 proteins/studies, unnamed FGFR2 source), k256_cipher (drops probe mean 0.496 -> 0.278), k256_flipped (exposes Rhomax prior reliance at +0.583), and k0_recall.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: All methods train on identically rounded prompt labels; exact-match pools separate discrete (nucb, rhomax) from continuous splits; Mythos subagent harness route is kept strictly separate from public API models.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct variant ranking without generative candidate filtering.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Zero tools or code execution permitted (verified via transcript audit); validation-selected low effort reported alongside high-effort sweep (+0.027, CI includes zero); API and subagent routes never mixed.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Nine ridge baselines across ESM-2 650M and ESMC 300M/600M/6B fit on identical 256 rows plus five negative controls; note best ridge is chosen on test queries (favoring baselines) and no fine-tuned ESMC baseline was run yet.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: All code, exact prompt files, model answers, audit scripts, and tables are publicly released; limitation: Mythos 5.2 ran 100 queries per split (1 draw, 1 answer) due to usage limits.

critiques_and_commentary.author: Anthony Gitter
critiques_and_commentary.summary: Cited as an exemplar of rigorous in-context controls and post-cutoff DMS curation in contrast to OpenAI's unaudited ProteinGym benchmark.

takeaway: With 256 labeled variants and no tools, Claude Mythos 5.2 ties the best ESMC ridge on both FLIP2 (0.380 vs 0.367) and a post-cutoff FGFR2 screen (0.561 vs 0.572), and averaging their rankings beats both (0.443 / 0.611). Prompt controls show roughly half the score comes from genuine in-context learning and half from prior protein knowledge, with Rhomax driven entirely by prior knowledge.
